questions.question: One agent plans, codes, and approves its own work with no separate review. What is missing?
options: A faster single agent
More tasks for the same agent
Blind trust in self-approval
Planner, builder, and an independent reviewer
questions.explanation: Self-approved work skips the very check that catches wrong-half fixes. This capstone separates the roles with handoffs between them.

questions.question: What is the reviewer's modeled probability of catching an injected bug?
questions.explanation: review_code uses a catch probability of 0.85; the complementary 0.15 is the modeled false-approval probability.

questions.question: What test result does the sample tester agent send after the final revision?
options: 412/412 passing
410/412 passing
5/10 passing
412/420 passing
questions.explanation: After the reviewer catches the injected bug and the coder revises, the tester posts the exact success message "412/412 passing".

questions.question: Which message handles a failed review in the team protocol?
options: TEST_PASS is sent directly to the product owner
REVIEW_FEEDBACK is routed to the coder, whose revision is reviewed again
BUG_FOUND closes the task without a revision
ARCHITECT_PLAN replaces the review with a fresh decomposition
questions.explanation: A negative review posts REVIEW_FEEDBACK; the coder fixes the reported bug and the reviewer performs the approval step again.

questions.question: What approval comparison is printed for the team run?
options: The team approves 5/10 while a single agent approves 7/10
Both approaches approve 7/10
The team approves 7/10 while the single-agent baseline approves 5/10
The baseline is not run, so no approval score is available
questions.explanation: The demo compares team approval=7/10 with the single-agent baseline=5/10, alongside the separate handoff and token metrics.

questions.question: What does the reported 1.60× token amplification compare?
options: The reviewer's catch rate with the tester's flake rate
The number of subtasks with the number of agents
The team's passing tests with the baseline's passing tests
The multi-agent token total with the single-agent token total
questions.explanation: The printed amplification compares the matched-trial means, 34,819 team tokens per run versus 21,705 baseline tokens per run, yielding 1.60×. The 35,530-token figure is the separate single demo run.
